added_failures_source.arms_green: both arms exit 0 over the same four gate files (33 passed at repair-gate-base.log rev 4b05b1d7, 35 passed at repair-gate-head.log rev dcb91f92); both logs re-read, and the reviewed base tree verified to carry 4b05b1d7's dispatch.py
added_failures_source.count_derivation: set difference of FAILED/ERROR node ids over the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite gate logs as named in its manifest, computed with review.added_failures_from_gate_logs
added_failures_source.read_time_view: annotate_review_of_run over the reviewed run's manifest resolves both arms - the repair converted the suite fields from prose to JSON carrying log_path, so the count reads 0 rather than the prior record's unmeasured None; the prior review's fourth finding is repaired

call_sites: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1423 (the grant helper adds the fragment paths)
reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4273 (peer scopes filtered against the shared set)

findings.text: the "Open, outside this node's fence: nine cases in four neighbouring test modules pin the retired default and were not in this node's write scope" bullet (duplicated at docs/evidence/archive/a-landing-record-never-conflicts-landed.html:31) is stale at the repair head: the repair commit touched neither landing record, yet two of those nine cases are in tests/test_context_estimate_excludes_granted_paths.py, which the run itself repaired at dcb91f92 and listed in changed_paths, and which passes in the 35-passed head arm, so the open set is seven cases in three modules and the parenthetical's "the last calling _grant_landing_write_paths without the new warnings argument" describes the pre-repair file; the bullet's own "See follow_ons in the run manifest" pointer now disagrees with a manifest that names three modules.

the "Gate arms: gate-base.log (base 4b05b1d7, 31 passing, exit 0) and gate-head.log (this tree, 33 passing, exit 0) over the three gate files" line (duplicated at docs/evidence/archive/a-landing-record-never-conflicts-landed.html:29) names the pre-repair arms, and neither landing record mentions the repair arms; the current evidence is repair-gate-base.log (33 passed at 4b05b1d7) and repair-gate-head.log (35 passed at dcb91f92) over four files, the pair the manifest's own suite fields name.

the figure sentence inside the rewritten PLAN_LANDING_CONTRACT still reads under docs/figures/<topic>/ while the FENCE - SCOPE block composed into the same prompt (prompts.py:396, node.write_paths) grants docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/, so a node following its own contract writes into the plan-wide figure directory - the shared path this change retired and the one whose explicit declaration _grant_landing_write_paths (dispatch.py:1411-1420) warns reintroduces the merge conflict.

the fragment join in the new _landing_fragment_paths is left in a three-line parenthesised form that ruff format collapses to one 88-character line; the region is added by this change - ruff format --diff reports eight hunks at head against seven at base, the extra being this site - against the repository rule that a commit adds no findings.

the assertion added to the fragment case (sorted write-path lists compared unequal) is left unformatted, ruff format collapsing :267-269 to one 86-character line; it is the second region this change adds, base's only hunk in this file being the pre-existing :110 hunk.

the command line meant to make the head arm re-runnable reads PYTHONPATH=<worktree> <venv-python> -m pytest with both placeholders unsubstituted, so the header names no path or interpreter a reader can execute; negative-control.log:4 carries the same form and gate-base.log:3 says exported from $REV, while repair-gate-base.log's header is fully resolved.

the tests: line writes the head interpreter as <root-.venv>/bin/python, so the field recording the gate command names no interpreter that resolves, and its PYTHONPATH=$PWD is a shell literal rather than the worktree path the head arm actually ran with.

item_verdicts.diff: two commits over base 4b05b1d7, ten files, +449/-162. f6e41cc7 lands the fragment default and the contract rewrite; dcb91f92 repairs the estimator grant and the test modules (+79/-62 over four files). Both carry conventional subjects and bodies and neither carries an AI-attribution trailer. Net lint delta over the seven touched Python files is zero (per-file counts identical at base and head, 22 aggregate) and the test module the prior review flagged as newly unformatted is formatted at head, but two regions the change added are newly unformatted (dispatch.py:1376, tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py:267).
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks for six dry-run nodes through the real dispatcher asserting no two default scopes contain or are contained in the same path, a prompt fixture, the redispatch and explicit-shared cases, exit 0 for the named test modules, arm logs whose headers print revision and reckon.__file__, and the declared negative control applied with its log path in the manifest. All are present at dcb91f92: tests/test_shared_landing_paths.py drives six nodes through dispatch.plan_dispatch with pairwise disjointness and its prompt fixture asserts the fragment present and the three shared paths absent; the repair added the estimator case in tests/test_context_estimate_excludes_granted_paths.py; the manifest records 33 passed at base and 35 at head, both exit 0, and I re-read both logs and verified the base tree's provenance (/tmp/base-tree2 dispatch.py sha256 7d3feda0 equals 4b05b1d7's blob); the negative control's first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim and its body shows the disjointness assertion failing with all fifteen pairs, exit 1.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to replace a node's three shared landing paths with its own fragment, and the repair head lands it across every production path: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1349 derives docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/<node-id>.html and docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/, :1389 grants them by default and warns (dispatch.py:1411-1420) when a declared path resolves into the retired set, reckon/crew/prompts.py:69 rewrites PLAN_LANDING_CONTRACT to the fragment and one landing: manifest line, and the repair moves reckon/crew/routing.py:1833 onto the same function dispatch grants from, so no production default still names a shared landing path. One loose end of the goal remains: the contract's figure sentence (prompts.py:76-78) still sends figures to docs/figures/<topic>/ while the FENCE - SCOPE block composed into the same prompt (prompts.py:396) grants the per-node directory.
item_verdicts.manifest: reads complete at head with status complete, both suite fields now resolvable JSON carrying log_path - the prior review's fourth finding is repaired, and annotate_review_of_run resolves both arms and measures this run's added failures as zero, empty - plus negative_control_log a bare path and follow_ons naming three modules. Blemishes: the tests: line writes the interpreter as <root-.venv> and the logs written in the repair round carry unsubstituted placeholders in the command header that exists to make them re-runnable (repair-gate-head.log:5, negative-control.log:4).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared fence holds six paths and the run changes ten. The four outside are disclosed at manifest.md:28 - tests/test_brief_prompt.py and tests/test_crew_dispatch_guard.py are required green at exit 0 by the node's own gate text and were edited at f6e41cc7, and reckon/crew/routing.py plus tests/test_context_estimate_excludes_granted_paths.py were edited at dcb91f92 under the coordinator's explicit repair authorization (resume-1-advice.txt: edit it anyway, the coordinator accepts that path at promotion). No path is touched undisclosed; the three docs edits are additive and no plan-version or plan-modified meta line is written.

justifications.durability: the disjointness assertion is proven sensitive twice over - the declared negative control reddens it in all fifteen node pairs (negative-control.log, exit 1) and a falsification reinstating the pre-repair estimator grant reddens both new estimator cases (gates/rev-falsify-estimator.log, 2 failed, exit 1) - so the guard the prior review found inert is now wired to the function dispatch grants from and pinned by a case that fails when the defect returns.
justifications.evidence: the gate's own measure is asserted and green (six-node pairwise disjointness through plan_dispatch, the prompt fixture, the redispatch and explicit-shared cases, plus the estimator case added in the repair), the manifest's suite fields are now resolvable JSON so annotate_review_of_run measures the added-failure count as zero over the reviewed run's own arms, and the base tree's provenance and both arm logs were re-read independently - but the landing records misstate the open set and name superseded arms, which a reader outside the run directory would take as current.
justifications.fit: the repair lands cleanly against the repository's lint rule - per-file ruff check counts are identical at base and head, 22 aggregate over the seven touched files, and the previously unformatted test module is formatted - but two regions the change added are newly unformatted and the repair's own log headers and manifest tests line carry unsubstituted placeholders, against the house convention that a record a reader can act on names real paths.
justifications.goal_fidelity: dispatch.py:1349 derives the fragment from the node id for every plan node, dispatch.py:1389 grants it by default and warns only when a coordinator declares a shared path, prompts.py:69 names the fragment and one landing: line, and the repair puts routing.py:1833 on the same function, so all three shared landing paths are out of every default scope in the production path; the figure sentence at prompts.py:76-78 is the one remaining contradiction with the per-node figure grant.
justifications.scope_discipline: ten changed paths against a six-path declared fence; the four extra are disclosed at manifest.md:28, two forced green by the node's own gate text and two edited in the repair round under the coordinator's explicit authorization, with no undisclosed path and no plan meta line touched.
